sources.entry: Challenging projects every programmer should try, Austin Z. Henley

summary.title: Challenging projects every programmer should try
summary.one_liner: A list of six hands-on software projects (text editor, 2D game, compiler, mini OS, spreadsheet, console emulator) and what each teaches, with suggested further reading.
takeaways: Building a text editor teaches text storage data structures (gap buffer, piece table, rope) and undo/redo via the Command pattern.
A 2D game project covers the game loop, input handling, object management with patterns like factory, and state machines for enemy AI.
A Tiny BASIC compiler can be written from scratch in a few days, covering lexing, recursive descent parsing, semantic checks and code generation.
Operating system, spreadsheet and console emulator projects are harder; start emulators with CHIP-8 before real consoles like NES or Game Boy.
The page also lists further project ideas such as a database, ray tracer, vector editor and FTP client.
summary.summary: The author, Austin Henley, presents a set of software projects he says taught him a lot and suggests building them multiple times. Each project section explains the core challenges (for example, cursor behavior and data structures for editors, the game loop for games, lexing and parsing for compilers) and lists things to learn and further reading. The post ends with a community-sourced list of additional project ideas and mentions the author's forthcoming e-book on similar projects, plus Amazon affiliate links.
